what: First physical-phone session: a person played both games in the Flutter host on a Samsung Galaxy S23 through the local stack

device.connection: USB, with adb reverse tcp:18080 so the phone's 127.0.0.1:18080 reached the Mac's gateway; no Wi-Fi or public network

app.note: Debug build; plain HTTP works only because Flutter's Gradle plugin adds usesCleartextTraffic to debug builds.
app.cleartext_correction: Corrected 2026-10-23: usesCleartextTraffic=true came from the app's own main manifest, where it had been since M1; Flutter's Gradle plugin does not add it. Release builds therefore also allowed cleartext until 2026-10-23, when the attribute was replaced by a network security config that allows cleartext in debug builds only (see evidence/android_release_https_2026-10-24.json).

stack: The disposable stack used for the load profile: PostgreSQL 18.6 on 127.0.0.1:55432, Redis 7.4.11 and Kafka 3.9.1 containers, the six Go services, the gateway on 127.0.0.1:18080 serving a fresh web/dist, and a new per-run secret that was not recorded.
observations: The project owner played Pulse Field with their own taps: the page showed 'Finished rhythm: 130 points' and the Flutter host's status bar showed 'rhythm: 130 points · taps: 39', so the bridge messages passed the host's parser.
They then switched to Comet Catch and played again: 'Finished reflex: 15 points', 12 taps.
SQL recorded both as accepted scores for phone1 (rhythm 130 in 10,007 ms; reflex 15 in 10,009 ms), with their outbox events published and processed.

With the app idle on the Comet Catch board, a second player scored 90 from the Mac through cmd/e2e-probe (200, then 409 for the replay; its own frame 6 ms after submission). The phone's in-app leaderboard updated to show it above phone1 with no input other than a scroll.
Final SQL: 4 accepted attempts (two from the phone, two scripted from the Mac), 4 scores, all outbox events published and processed, daily accepted 4.
screenshots: Not kept: the phone's screenshots showed a messaging app's chat-head overlay with a personal photo.
limits: One phone over USB to the Mac's loopback, not a mobile network.
Debug build over plain HTTP; no release build or HTTPS.
Demo user ID supplied by the host; no authenticated identity.
